title.en: England striker Ivan Toney charged with assault after Soho nightclub incident
title.zh: 英格兰前锋伊万·托尼在苏豪夜总会事件后被控袭击罪

summary.en: England striker Ivan Toney has been charged with assault following an alleged incident at a Soho nightclub in London. The Metropolitan police confirmed the charge against the 30-year-old from Northampton.
summary.zh: 英格兰前锋伊万·托尼在伦敦苏豪区一家夜总会发生的一起涉嫌袭击事件后被指控犯有袭击罪。大都会警察局证实了对这位来自北安普顿的30岁球员的指控。

body.en:
The England striker Ivan Toney has been charged with assault after an incident at a nightclub in Soho.

The Metropolitan police said Toney, 30, of Northampton, was charged on 31 July with assault causing actual bodily harm.

The force said the charge relates to an alleged assault that reportedly took place on 6 December last year at a nightclub on Wardour Street in central London.

Toney, a striker for Saudi Pro League club Al-Ahli, will appear at Westminster magistrates court on 24 September.

The Sun newspaper reported on 8 December that Toney had been arrested after an alleged head-butt.

A spokesperson for Toney said: “Ivan acknowledges the charge and although he is naturally shocked, he looks forward to being given the opportunity to clear his name in court.”
body.zh: 英格兰前锋伊万·托尼在苏豪区一家夜总会发生事件后被指控袭击。 大都会警方表示，30 岁的北安普顿人伊万·托尼 (Ivan Toney) 于 7 月 31 日被指控袭击造成实际身体伤害。 警方表示，这项指控与据称去年 12 月 6 日在伦敦市中心沃杜尔街一家夜总会发生的袭击事件有关。 托尼是沙特职业联赛俱乐部阿赫利队的前锋，他将于 9 月 24 日在威斯敏斯特地方法院出庭。 《太阳报》12 月 8 日报道称，托尼因涉嫌用头撞人而被捕。 托尼的发言人表示：“伊万承认这一指控，尽管他自然感到震惊，但他期待有机会在法庭上洗清自己的罪名。”

reflection.en: When allegations arise, especially involving public figures, it is easy to form quick judgments based on initial reports. Yahweh's wisdom reminds us to listen carefully to all sides before reaching conclusions, allowing due process to unfold. This approach fosters fairness and resists the urge to rush to judgment.
reflection.zh: 当指控出现时，尤其涉及公众人物时，人们很容易根据初步报道迅速做出判断。雅伟的智慧提醒我们，在得出结论之前要仔细倾听各方意见，让正当程序得以进行。这种做法促进了公平，并抵制了仓促下结论的冲动。

title.en: Meta fined $567m in largest child safety ruling against social media giant
title.zh: Meta 在针对社交媒体巨头的最大儿童安全裁决中被罚款 5.67 亿美元

summary.en: The ruling is in addition to $375m in fines Meta was already ordered to pay in the case, for a total of $942m.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及真理、分辨与诚实。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
A US judge in New Mexico has ordered Meta to pay another $567m (£421m) for its failure to warn the public about dangers its platforms posed to children, marking the largest fine against the company over child safety.

Judge Bryan Biedscheid said the social media giant is a "public nuisance" akin to air pollution and that it must put the money in a fund aimed at reducing future harms.

Thursday's ruling is in addition to $375m in fines Meta was already ordered to pay in the case, for a total of $942m.

Judge Biedscheid compared Meta to a factory, with advertising and content as its product and "the psychological harm and sexual exploitation of children to be the pollution that must be abated".

A spokesman for Meta, which owns and operates Instagram, Facebook, WhatsApp and Threads, said Thursday: "We disagree with the ruling and will appeal."

"We work hard to keep people safe on our platforms and have been transparent about the challenges of identifying and removing bad actors and harmful content," they added.

"We remain confident in our record of protecting teens online and will continue to defend ourselves against claims that misrepresent the facts."

Regarding the earlier $375m verdict in the case, Meta had said it intended to appeal the ruling and gave a similar explanation. It was the first time that a state had successfully sued Meta over child safety issues.

Meta is currently facing thousands of lawsuits in the US over similar issues. In addition to the New Mexico rulings, Meta earlier this year lost a landmark case in Los Angeles which found it could be held liable for building addictive platforms .

Bruce Daisley, a former European vice president of Twitter (now X), told BBC Radio 4's Today programme the New Mexico fine, while large, was "a drop in the ocean" for Meta.

In its latest financial results , the social media giant posted $61bn in revenue from April to June - up 28% on the same period a year ago.

"But it's an indication that we are moving to a stage where social media is going to be tackled around the world," he said.

Meanwhile, former safeguarding minister Jess Phillips told Today she believed US court challenges against big tech could enable the UK to take tougher action - without fearing it may damage UK-US diplomatic ties.

It argued Meta should be held liable for the way in which its platforms endangered children and exposed them to sexually explicit material and contact with sexual predators.

In the first phase of the trial, Meta was found to have repeatedly violated New Mexico's Unfair Practices Act as its recommendation algorithms essentially "steered" young users toward harmful content and contacts.

body.zh: 新墨西哥州的一名美国法官因 Meta 未能就其平台对儿童构成的危险向公众发出警告而下令其再支付 5.67 亿美元（4.21 亿英镑），这是该公司在儿童安全问题上收到的最大一笔罚款。 法官布莱恩·比德沙伊德 (Bryan Biedscheid) 表示，这家社交媒体巨头是一种类似于空气污染的“公害”，它必须将这笔钱投入一个旨在减少未来危害的基金。 除了周四的裁决外，Meta 还被勒令在此案中支付 3.75 亿美元的罚款，总计 9.42 亿美元。 Biedscheid法官将Meta比作一家工厂，以广告和内容为产品，“对儿童的心理伤害和性剥削是必须减少的污染”。 拥有并运营 Instagram、Facebook、WhatsApp 和 Threads 的 Meta 发言人周四表示：“我们不同意这一裁决，并将上诉。” 他们补充说：“我们努力确保人们在我们平台上的安全，并对识别和删除不良行为者和有害内容的挑战保持透明。” “我们对保护青少年上网的记录仍然充满信心，并将继续针对歪曲事实的指控为自己辩护。” 对于此前该案3.75亿美元的判决，Meta曾表示打算上诉，并给出了类似的解释。这是第一次有州就儿童安全问题成功起诉 Meta。 Meta 目前在美国因类似问题面临数千起诉讼。除了新墨西哥州的裁决之外，Meta 今年早些时候在洛杉矶败诉了一起具有里程碑意义的案件，该案件发现它可能因建立令人上瘾的平台而承担责任。 Twitter 前欧洲副总裁 Bruce Daisley（现为 X）告诉 BBC Radio 4 的 Today 节目，新墨西哥州的罚款虽然数额巨大，但对 Meta 来说只是“沧海一粟”。 在最新的财务业绩中，这家社交媒体巨头公布 4 月至 6 月的收入为 610 亿美元，比去年同期增长 28%。 “但这表明我们正在进入一个全球范围内都将应对社交媒体问题的阶段，”他说。 与此同时，前安全大臣杰西·菲利普斯 (Jess Phillips) 告诉《今日报》，她相信美国法院对大型科技公司提出的挑战可能会让英国采取更强硬的行动，而不必担心这可能会损害英美外交关系。 它认为 Meta 应该对其平台危害儿童、让他们接触露骨色情材料以及与性掠夺者接触的方式承担责任。 在审判的第一阶段，Meta 被发现多次违反新墨西哥州的不公平行为法，因为其推荐算法本质上“引导”年轻用户接触有害内容和联系人。 推荐算法是 Meta 用来自动管理用户在其网站上看到的内容的工具。

title.en: Thai teen kills eight in shooting rampage at school and home
title.zh: 泰国少年在学校和家中枪杀八人

summary.en: Police have identified a student as the perpetrator of a shooting rampage at a school and home in Thailand, which resulted in eight deaths.
summary.zh: 警方已确认一名学生是泰国一所学校和家中枪击事件的肇事者，该事件造成八人死亡。

body.en:
A teenage suspect killed his grandparents before shooting dead at least six more people at a school near Bangkok on Friday, police said.

First, he shot dead his grandparents, using his grandfather's handgun, then went to a secondary school north of Bangkok and killed three teachers and three students, national police said in a statement.

Dozens of police and emergency responders gathered outside the Debsirin Nonthaburi School in Nonthaburi province on Friday, while parents raced to pick up their children and tearful students and staff comforted each other outside.

"I was afraid that I would die, and I was scared that I wouldn't be able to pursue my dreams," said Pawarisa Maylissa, a grade 12 student who hopes to attend medical school.

"I heard many gunshots very loudly because it seemed the suspect was on the floor directly above us. I could even hear bullets hitting the floor."

Fifteen injured students were not struck by gunfire but hurt as they were trying to flee, deputy interior minister Polapee Suwunchwee told local broadcaster Thai PBS.

The shooter was identified as a teenage student of the school and also reported dead, according to local media reports citing authorities.

One 18-year-old student told the Reuters news agency he initially thought there were firecrackers going off or someone banging an object.

"I didn't think it was a gun at first," he said. "There were many shots: bang bang bang. Then it went quiet. Then it started again."

Some reports said police officers had shot and killed the suspect, while others said he had died by suicide.

"It's such a terrible incident. It should never have happened. How could this happen in our country?" Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul told reporters at Bangkok's Government House.

Photos published by local media show the suspect wearing a purple school uniform and carrying a black cross-body bag, with several bullet casings visible on the ground.

It is the second school shooting in Thailand this year after a teacher died and a student was injured in the south of the country in February.

Emergency worker Kiatikhun Verapongpradith, 47, described arriving as the shooting was ongoing and his team treated students with injuries in the back, chest and arms.

They found a male teacher lying dead on an upper floor of the school, and in another room they found a female teacher with wounds in her chest and arm.

"We gave CPR for about 30 minutes and rushed her to the hospital as we could not get her heart rate up, but we tried our best," he said.

title.en: German airport drone-bomb: Could Russia be involved?
title.zh: 德国机场无人机炸弹袭击：俄罗斯可能参与其中吗？

summary.en: The BBC has seen evidence from previous cases that Russian-linked proxies not only handled drones and explosives, but also delivered them to Germany.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
As Germany investigates how a drone loaded with explosives reached a runway at Leipzig airport, there is renewed talk in Europe of hybrid war.

The interior minister is warning of a "new level of danger" from an attack that "may involve foreign powers".

There is no proof at this stage to link the flying bomb directly to Russia, which denies any role. But as well as the means and the motive, Moscow does have form.

The BBC has seen details of the investigation into a plot in 2024 in which Russian-linked proxies in Poland and Lithuania not only handled drones and explosives but also delivered them to Germany.

The quadcopter was discovered at Leipzig airport late on Tuesday night, forcing one runway into lockdown as a bomb disposal robot rolled into action.

On the tarmac close by were several Ukrainian Antonov cargo planes, stripes along their enormous bodies in the blue and yellow of the country's flag. One reads, "Be Brave Like Kherson", the southern city now on the frontline of Russia's invasion.

Pictures published by German media suggest the drone was a relatively small device which airport staff spotted "floating" between the Ukrainian planes.

Around the same time, a DHL cargo plane collided with an "unidentified object" as it pulled up into the sky, unable to land in Leipzig.

In 2024, a parcel containing a sophisticated incendiary device caught fire at the airport's DHL hub shortly before it was loaded onto a plane. Similar packages then ignited in the UK and Poland, causing extensive damage.

A group of men are currently on trial in both Lithuania and Poland, where prosecutors believe they were part of a substantial network of proxies recruited by Russian military intelligence.

Last September, Lithuanian prosecutors said that investigators had also seized RDX explosives meant for "other terrorist attacks". The amount was significant: equivalent to 6kg of TNT.

"Some of the devices were manufactured to intensify the blast," the prosecutor added.

The BBC has since had access to case documents that describe how several of the men on trial were paid to transport those explosives around Europe, concealed in cans of sweetcorn and chopped tomatoes. The detonators were hidden inside headphone sets.

The suspects also handled drone parts and the case talks specifically of attachments, suitable for holding a bomb.

Prosecutors allege that some of the items were brought into the EU from the Russian exclave of Kaliningrad.

Almost two dozen suspects have been charged with terror offences, but with the men's handlers still at large, believed to be in Russia, it is not clear whether the entire network was disbanded or all the hidden material found.

body.zh: 当德国调查一架载有炸药的无人机如何抵达莱比锡机场跑道时，欧洲重新开始谈论混合战争。 内政部长警告说，“可能涉及外国势力”的袭击将造成“新的危险”。 现阶段没有证据表明这枚飞行炸弹与俄罗斯直接相关，俄罗斯否认有任何作用。但除了手段和动机之外，莫斯科也有形式。 BBC 看到了对 2024 年一起阴谋的调查细节，在该阴谋中，波兰和立陶宛与俄罗斯有联系的代理人不仅处理无人机和爆炸物，还将它们运送到德国。 周二深夜，这架四轴飞行器在莱比锡机场被发现，导致一条跑道被迫封锁，一台拆弹机器人投入使用。 附近的停机坪上有几架乌克兰安东诺夫货机，巨大的机身上有乌克兰国旗的蓝色和黄色条纹。其中一张写着“像赫尔松一样勇敢”，这座南部城市现在正处于俄罗斯入侵的前线。 德国媒体发布的图片显示，这架无人机是一个相对较小的设备，机场工作人员发现它“漂浮”在乌克兰飞机之间。 大约在同一时间，一架DHL货机在升空时与“不明物体”相撞，无法降落在莱比锡。 2024 年，一个装有复杂燃烧装置的包裹在装上飞机前不久在机场的 DHL 枢纽着火。类似的包裹随后在英国和波兰被点燃，造成了广泛的损失。 一群男子目前正在立陶宛和波兰接受审判，检察官认为他们是俄罗斯军事情报部门招募的庞大代理人网络的一部分。 去年9月，立陶宛检察官表示，调查人员还查获了用于“其他恐怖袭击”的RDX炸药。数量巨大：相当于6公斤TNT。 检察官补充说：“有些装置是为了加强爆炸而制造的。” 此后，英国广播公司获得了案件文件，其中描述了几名受审男子如何获得报酬，将这些爆炸物藏在甜玉米罐头和切碎的西红柿中运送到欧洲各地。雷管隐藏在耳机内。 嫌疑人还处理了无人机零件，案件特别提到了适合放置炸弹的附件。 检察官声称，其中一些物品是从俄罗斯飞地加里宁格勒带入欧盟的。 近两打嫌疑人被指控犯有恐怖罪，但这些人的操纵者仍然在逃，据信在俄罗斯，目前尚不清楚整个网络是否已被解散或所有隐藏材料是否已被发现。 虽然没有证据表明与莱比锡无人机炸弹有关，但 2024 年的阴谋无疑凸显了……

title.en: A new youth agitation grips an Indian state after 'cockroach' protests
title.zh: “蟑螂”抗议后，印度各邦掀起了新的青年骚乱

summary.en: Weeks after the CJP protests shook Delhi, a new youth-led movement over jobs and recruitment is gathering force in Jharkhand.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Weeks after thousands of young Indians poured onto the streets of Delhi in a major 'cockroach' protest over examination paper leaks , another group of frustrated job seekers is making headlines - this time hundreds of miles away, in the eastern state of Jharkhand.

Protesters have gathered at a stadium in the state capital Ranchi, since 25 July, demanding an overhaul of the state's government examination system. Some have been sleeping in the open and several have gone on hunger strike.

The 27-year-old, from a farming family from Bokaro, has spent years preparing for Jharkhand's civil service examination, hoping it would get her the security of a government job. She has already sat the exam three times and hoped to get a good score this time.

"We want justice. We will not leave until we get it, even if it costs us our lives," she said.

The immediate cause of the anger is a preliminary civil service examination held in April.

After the results were announced in July, candidates alleged that leaked answer sheets shared on social media showed some successful applicants had answered far fewer questions than expected.

This fuelled suspicions that the results had been manipulated. The protesters want the exam scrapped and held again. They also want the case investigated by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), India's premier federal investigative agency.

The allegations are being investigated by Jharkhand's Criminal Investigation Department (CID) and the Jharkhand Public Service Commission has since postponed the next stage of the examination. Its chairman, L Khiangte, resigned on 22 July and has been questioned as part of the investigation.

Investigators are also examining the role of a private company that conducted parts of the examination process, after candidates raised questions about how it was selected.

Deepika Pandey Singh, a minister in the Jharkhand government, told the BBC that the state had begun investigating the allegations even before the current protest.

She urged protesters to let the CID complete its investigation instead of handing the case to the CBI. "We want a fair investigation," she said, adding that anyone responsible - "whether a bureaucrat, employee, middleman or a big politician" - would face action. She also said the government would discuss the protesters' demand to cancel the April exam with them directly.

But protesters say their fight goes beyond one exam. They want a wider probe into alleged recruitment irregularities, action against those responsible and long-delayed hiring completed on time. Above all, they want regular, transparent exams so candidates are no longer left waiting indefinitely.

title.en: Moment earthquake shakes hospital operating room in Japan
title.zh: 地震瞬间日本医院手术室摇晃

summary.en: Security camera footage from Kumamoto General Hospital in Japan captured the moment a magnitude 6.8 earthquake struck an operating room last month. The video shows medical staff quickly shielding a patient on the operating table from the shaking.
summary.zh: 日本熊本综合医院的监控录像捕捉到上个月一场6.8级地震袭击手术室的瞬间。视频显示，医护人员迅速遮挡手术台上的病人，以保护其免受震动。

body.en:
Newly-released security camera footage shows the moment last month's magnitude 6.8 quake shook Kumamoto General Hospital in Japan.

Four surgeries were under way at the time. Footage from a camera in an operating room where an abdominal surgery was being performed shows medical staff shielding the patient with their bodies as equipment swayed violently, and a nurse opening a door to secure an evacuation route.

Kumamoto General Hospital resumed normal outpatient services on 5 August , after suspending them following the earthquake on 28 July.
body.zh: 新发布的监控录像显示了上个月发生的 6.8 级地震震撼日本熊本综合医院的瞬间。 当时正在进行四次手术。正在进行腹部手术的手术室中的摄像机拍摄的视频显示，当设备剧烈摇晃时，医护人员用身体保护病人，护士打开门以确保疏散路线。 熊本综合医院在 7 月 28 日地震后暂停门诊服务，并于 8 月 5 日恢复正常门诊服务。

Yahweh is indeed our refuge and strength, a constant help when the world...

title.en: Australian aviation crew carries out daring midwinter Antarctica rescue
title.zh: 澳大利亚航空机组人员在南极洲进行大胆的隆冬救援

summary.en: An Australian aviation team successfully evacuated a patient from McMurdo Station in Antarctica. The rescue involved landing a plane in complete darkness and temperatures of -43°C during the midwinter period.
summary.zh: 一支澳大利亚航空团队成功地从南极麦克默多站撤离了一名病人。这次救援行动是在隆冬时节，完全黑暗、零下43摄氏度的极端条件下着陆飞机完成的。

body.en:
An Australian aviation crew has carried out a daring midwinter mission to rescue a US expedition member from a station in Antarctica in freezing temperatures and total darkness.

Skytraders said the "extraordinary" mission took place last Friday after a request for urgent help with a medical evacuation from McMurdo Station.

After an initial delay due to the weather, the aviation company said it was able to land its Airbus A319 in "extremely challenging conditions" including temperatures of -43C (-45.4F).

The patient was then safely transferred onto the plane, known as Snowbird 1, which carried on to Christchurch in New Zealand, where the patient was treated. He is now recovering well.

Captain Louise Robertson, one of four pilots on the flight which took off from the Tasmanian city of Hobart, told the BBC it was the first ever to have taken place in July and to be completed in total darkness.

"We completed it on the 31 July, and the first day of any sort of sunlight, which was very minimal, would be on the 1 August," she said.

Her husband of 18 years, Rod Robertson, was the pilot who landed the plane at the US research station on Ross Island.

"He was in the left seat and I was in the right seat," she said, adding that it was the most complex operation she had ever been involved in during her seven years at Skytraders and 25 as a pilot.

Skytraders had received the evacuation request from the US Antarctic Program via the Australian Antarctic Division on Wednesday afternoon, Robertson said.

It was a "major operation" for the plane to be correctly configured in time by engineers and a design team, who fitted a stretcher in the back.

The configuration took 24 hours, Robertson said, but takeoff was then delayed for another 12 hours while the crew waited for a suitable window in the weather.

"We had quite a narrow time frame that we could actually fly down to Antarctica because there was a snowstorm on the first day that we were intending to go down which stopped the operation."

The storm prevented crew at the station from getting to the runway, made of compacted snow, which had to be graded and groomed to make it smooth - a six-hour job.

The ground crew "did a phenomenal job to make a 3-km-long runway available for us given the conditions they were also facing, -45C and strong wind," Robertson said.

The flight crew spent exactly one hour on the ground at Phoenix Airfield before taking off again for Christchurch.

title.en: Why one tiny island's Census is about much more than numbers
title.zh: 为什么一个小岛的人口普查不仅仅是数字

summary.en: It's been a decade since Norfolk Island was first counted in the Census. The milestone may not be celebrated by everyone.

body.en:
In the middle of the South Pacific Ocean, a tiny island spanning just 35 square kilometres will be included in this year's Census .

Home to about 2,100 residents, Norfolk Island has earned a reputation as "one of the most beautiful places on Earth", according to acting general manager of the Norfolk Island Regional Council (NIRC), Nicholas Mostardo.

He moved to the subtropical island early this year and says its natural beauty and close-knit community make it unlike anywhere else.

"It's got a rich environment, it's got very warm and kind people. It's probably one of the most unique places in the world that I've had personally the pleasure of being involved with," Mostardo told SBS News.

NIRC is currently under administration until 31 December 2026, as Norfolk Island transitions to what the Australian government has described as a "new bespoke governance model".

In the interim, Mostardo has been liaising with the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) to help ensure Norfolk Island's population is recorded during the Census of Population and Housing on 11 August.

"We've had several visits from the ABS zone manager and the assistant director of Census Mainstream and Enumeration. They've been coming out to ensure the community is well engaged and consulted on completing the form."

The Census has been conducted in Australia for more than a century , but this will be the third time Norfolk Island has ever participated in the survey. It also marks a decade since the Australian government passed reforms that led to the island being included in the Census.

In 1914, Norfolk became an Australian territory, but the "precise constitutional arrangement was not clear at the time", according to an online statement by legal advisory firm Norfolk Advisory.

Around 65 years later, the Australian parliament allowed Norfolk Islanders to form a limited self-government. Following governance reforms passed in 2015 and implemented in 2016, the Australian government assumed responsibility for the island's governance.

In 2023, Norfolk Island regained some involvement in its affairs through the establishment of a new advisory body, the Norfolk Island Governance Committee. The island is now considered an external territory of Australia.

This complex history has divided some people — including those of Pitcairn descent — about whether Norfolk Island should be counted during Australia's Census.

title.en: 'We had no intention': Israeli ambassador defends rare move on Labor platform
title.zh: “我们无意”：以色列大使为工党平台上罕见的举动辩护

body.en:
Israel's ambassador to Australia has defended his embassy's unusual public intervention ahead of Labor's national conference last month, rejecting suggestions it sought to influence the party's platform and insisting it was merely providing information to decision-makers.

In a rare step, the Israeli embassy issued a lengthy statement ahead of the conference in Adelaide, taking issue with Labor's proposed position on the Israeli-Palestinian conflict.

The embassy argued Labor's draft national platform placed responsibility for the conflict on Israel while overlooking the role of Hamas and Palestinian leadership.

It sparked criticism from pro-Palestinian advocates that Israel was inappropriately interfering in Australian politics.

Speaking to SBS Hebrew on Thursday, Israeli ambassador Hillel Newman said "we had no intention and no actual intervention".

"All we did was we put forth facts for the decision-makers to have before them in making educated decisions," he said.

"We are just a resource of some kind in giving the information. We did not intervene in the convention itself. We do not intervene in the process. We just brought information to the knowledge of the decision-makers.

"The Palestinian envoys here also had some things to say about the ALP platform and convention, and no-one said it's foreign intervention," he said.

At the time, the Australia Palestine Advocacy Network (APAN), an advocacy group, condemned what it called an "extraordinary intervention" by the Israeli embassy and described it as "an unacceptable attempt by a foreign government to influence Australia’s domestic political processes".

"If the Israeli regime believes Labor's platform is too critical while Gaza is being destroyed, perhaps it should reflect on its own conduct rather than attempting to pressure an Australian political party," APAN president Nasser Mashni said.

Mashni said the draft platform fell "far short of taking appropriate action to recognise the Palestinian genocide".

Israel has been accused of genocide by a United Nations inquiry, an allegation it denies. Its prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, is the subject of an International Criminal Court (ICC) arrest warrant over alleged war crimes and crimes against humanity, which Israel rejects.

The Labor platform is debated at its national conference to determine the party's positions on a broad range of issues. Its 2026 draft reflected shifts and an expanded position on Israel and Palestine since its last iteration in 2023.

The government decided to recognise Palestinian statehood in September last year.

title.en: The growing Russian threat giving Ukraine only seconds to react
title.zh: 俄罗斯日益增长的威胁让乌克兰只有几秒钟的反应时间

summary.en: Ukraine is facing an escalating threat from Russian ballistic missiles, with its defensive capabilities reportedly in short supply, leaving little time to react to incoming attacks.
summary.zh: 乌克兰正面临俄罗斯弹道导弹日益增长的威胁，据报道其防御能力严重不足，对来袭的袭击几乎没有反应时间。

body.en:
When Russia fires a ballistic missile at Ukraine, air defence systems have only minutes — sometimes seconds — to detect and intercept the deadly threat.

The lack of time has left Kyiv and other Ukrainian cities increasingly exposed to devastating attacks by the missiles that come down so fast and so steeply that Ukraine says only the United States-made Patriot defence system can stop them. But Ukraine says it has too few batteries and interceptors to protect itself.

Unlike cruise missiles, which behave like pilotless planes, ballistic missiles are launched like rockets and then dive steeply toward their targets at several times the speed of sound.

That sharply reduces the time available to find and destroy a warhead. The result has been repeated attacks like the latest barrage on the Ukrainian capital that targeted a brewery, a warehouse and a mail-sorting office. At least 17 people were killed and dozens more wounded in the attack on Wednesday, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said.

When the warhead is hurled toward its target, "it’s very, very steep and it’s going at a ridiculous speed", according to Thomas Withington, an expert on electronic warfare at the Royal United Services Institute, who compared the physics to playing catch. If the ball is "going really fast, it's harder to catch".

Russia's ground-launched Iskander-M missile is its main ballistic missile. Another example is the air-launched Kinzhal missile. Russia has also fired S-300 and S-400 air-defence missiles at ground targets. A model known as the Zircon is technically a hypersonic anti-ship cruise missile, but its high speed resembles that of a ballistic missile and creates a similar interception problem.

Here's a look at the challenge of shielding Ukraine from some of Russia's deadliest projectiles.

The most capable Patriot system supplied to Ukraine is designed for high-speed missile defence. Instead of exploding near a target, the PAC-3 system uses a manoeuvrable interceptor designed to collide with an incoming warhead. The Patriot technology must track the missile, predict its path and launch within minutes, sometimes leaving seconds for the final engagement.

Patriots are currently the only system in Ukrainian service capable of intercepting the Russian Iskander-M, S-400 and Zircon missiles, according to Ukrainian Air Force spokesperson Yurii Ihnat. The US and its allies operate other anti-ballistic systems, including THAAD and sea-based Aegis defences, but they have not been provided to Ukraine.

title.zh: 埃博拉：非洲疾控中心计划在疫情蔓延之际使用针对不同毒株的疫苗

summary.en: The head of the Africa Centres for Disease Control announced plans to use a vaccine developed for a different Ebola strain to combat the current outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo, following promising test results.
summary.zh: 非洲疾病控制中心负责人宣布，计划在刚果民主共和国当前的埃博拉疫情中使用针对此前埃博拉毒株开发的疫苗，初步测试显示该疫苗可能提供挽救生命的保护。

body.zh: 非洲疾病控制中心负责人承诺在当前刚果民主共和国疫情中部署针对先前埃博拉病毒株的疫苗，测试病例表明可能达到挽救生命的保护水平。 非洲卫生当局表示，他们将开始使用针对先前扎伊尔埃博拉病毒株的疫苗来治疗当前的疫情，该病毒株涉及另一种快速传播的病毒株，称为 Bundibugyo。目前的疫情集中在刚果民主共和国 (DRC) 东部。 非洲疾病控制中心（非洲疾病预防控制中心）总干事让·卡塞亚（Jean Kaseya）在周四的视频会议上告诉记者，在迄今为止进行的测试病例中，有证据表明该疫苗即使没有消除症状，也可以消除死亡。 非洲疾病预防控制中心和世界卫生组织还计划开展研究，检查当前疫情中可能存在的突变或其他异常情况，因为该病毒的传播速度比以往有记录的任何疫情爆发的速度都要快六到八倍。 这些警告是在受灾最严重的地区持续举行罢工和抗议之际，一些医务人员抱怨没有付款或工资和条件不足。 卡塞亚是在前一天在金沙萨会见世界卫生组织总干事谭德塞后在邻国刚果共和国的布拉柴维尔发表此番言论的。 非洲疾病预防控制中心负责人表示，鉴于最新数据截至周二已确诊 3,973 例，当局估计目前已确诊 4,000 例病例。该数据还表明，有 1,801 人确诊死于埃博拉病毒。目前的爆发是在五月中旬才宣布的，并且已经是有记录以来的第二大爆发。 与 2014 年至 2016 年发生的被认为是有史以来最大规模的西非疫情相比，当前菌株造成的死亡速度快了 6 倍。 卡塞亚说：“正如谭德塞博士昨天与我分享的那样，现在是世界卫生组织和非洲疾病预防控制中心进行研究以检查是否存在问题、是否存在其他问题，或者病毒是否没有变异的时候了，因为本迪布焦疫情的严重程度是前所未有的。” 卡塞亚表示，目前已有 51 个卫生区记录了病例，而 5 月份有 9 个。 他还提请注意确定的病例数量占接触者追踪计划规模的一部分。 2018 年至 2020 年期间，刚果民主共和国爆发了有记录以来毒性最强、致命性最强的扎伊尔菌株疫情，每 57 名被确定为高危接触者中就有一名患者被确诊。 在边境另一边的乌干达，该国表示已消除了今年出现的少量病例，名单上的每 41 名接触者中平均就有 1 例确诊病例。 在刚果民主共和国这...

reflection.en: In the face of a spreading disease, the efforts to deploy a vaccine offer a tangible sign of hope and care for the sick. This reminds us of the biblical call to pray for those afflicted by illness and to seek their healing. Yahweh hears the cries of those who suffer and works through human hands to bring relief.
reflection.zh: 面对蔓延的疾病，部署疫苗的努力为病患带来了切实的希望和关怀。这提醒我们圣经中为受疾病困扰者祷告并寻求他们医治的呼召。雅伟垂听受苦者的呼求，并借着人的手带来缓解。

verse.textEn: Is anyone among you sick? Let them call the elders of the church to pray over them.
verse.textZh: 你们中间有病了的呢，他就该请教会的长老来；他们可以奉主的名用油抹他，为他祷告。

title.en: How drought threatens electricity supplies in Europe
title.zh: 旱灾如何威胁欧洲电力供应

summary.en: Droughts, heatwaves, and critically low water levels in the Danube River are severely impacting central and southeastern Europe, leading to an energy crisis in countries like Hungary and Romania, while others such as Bulgaria have shown better preparedness.
summary.zh: 欧洲中部和东南部正遭受旱灾、热浪和多瑙河水位下降的严重影响。匈牙利和罗马尼亚面临能源危机，而保加利亚等国则准备得更充分。

body.en:
Droughts, heat and falling water levels in the Danube are hitting central and southeastern Europe hard. Hungary and Romania are experiencing an energy crisis — whereas countries like Bulgaria are better prepared.

Riverbeds reduced to tiny streams, asphalt melting like butter, dried-up fields — these are currently the images of drought in Central and Southeastern Europe. The record-breaking lack of rainfall in recent months and this summer's heatwaves have caused severe damage to the region's economy and infrastructure. 

In the agriculture sector, it has been clear for some time that harvests in Southeastern Europe, especially maize and sunflower crops, will be significantly below average. The heatwaves are also repeatedly disrupting road, rail and, above all, shipping transport. But, most importantly, the drought has triggered an unprecedented crisis in electricity generation in several Central and Southeastern European countries, forcing companies to halt production due to the historically low water level of the Danube.

Hungary and Romania are currently most affected by the energy crisis. Other countries bordering the Danube —  Austria , Slovakia , Serbia and Bulgaria  — are also suffering from low water levels, although not as severely as Hungary and Romania.

DW outlines the situation in each country and explains why, despite facing similar weather conditions, some are more severely affected than others.

No country in the region is currently as severely affected by drought and heat as Hungary. For months, there has been little or no rainfall in large parts of the country. On Wednesday, temperatures reached 43 degrees Celsius (109.4 degrees Fahrenheit) in the capital Budapest , and exceeded 40 degrees in many places across the country.

Due to the record-low water levels of the Danube, the Paks  nuclear power plant south of Budapest had to largely shut down operations, as there is no longer sufficent cooling water available and the temperature of the Danube water is too high. The plant is currently operating at around 12% of its capacity. If Danube water levels continue to drop, the plant will have to be shut down completely.

Due to the energy crisis, the Hungarian government has been urging large energy consumers to conserve electricity. As a result, several car manufacturers, including Audi Gyor, oil and gas company MOL and other large companies have scaled back production. Hungary's energy crisis — the worst in decades — is so severe because of the country's unfavorable energy mix. body.zh: 干旱、高温和多瑙河水位下降正在严重打击中欧和东南欧。匈牙利和罗马尼亚正在经历能源危机，而保加利亚等国家则做好了更充分的准备。 河床变成了细小的溪流，沥青像黄油一样融化，田地干涸——这些都是目前中欧和东南欧干旱的景象。近几个月破纪录的降雨不足和今年夏天的热浪对该地区的经济和基础设施造成了严重破坏。 在农业领域，一段时间以来，东南欧的收成，特别是玉米和向日葵作物的收成，将明显低于平均水平。热浪还一再扰乱公路、铁路，尤其是航运。但最重要的是，干旱在一些中欧和东南欧国家引发了前所未有的发电危机，迫使企业因多瑙河水位处于历史低位而停止生产。 匈牙利和罗马尼亚目前受能源危机影响最严重。多瑙河沿岸的其他国家——奥地利、斯洛伐克、塞尔维亚和保加利亚——也面临着低水位的问题，尽管没有匈牙利和罗马尼亚那么严重。 德国之声概述了每个国家的情况，并解释了为什么尽管面临相似的天气条件，但有些国家比其他国家受到的影响更严重。 该地区目前没有哪个国家像匈牙利一样受到干旱和高温的严重影响。几个月来，该国大部分地区降雨很少或根本没有降雨。周三，首都布达佩斯气温达到 43 摄氏度（109.4 华氏度），全国多地气温超过 40 度。 由于多瑙河水位创历史新低，布达佩斯以南的帕克斯核电站不得不大部分关闭，因为不再有足够的冷却水，而且多瑙河水温过高。该工厂目前的产能利用率约为 12%。如果多瑙河水位继续下降，该工厂将不得不完全关闭。 由于能源危机，匈牙利政府一直敦促能源大户节约用电。因此，包括奥迪杰尔 (Audi Gyor)、石油天然气公司 MOL 和其他大公司在内的多家汽车制造商都缩减了产量。匈牙利的能源危机——几十年来最严重的一次——之所以如此严重，是因为该国的能源结构不利。 Paks 生产的电力约占匈牙利发电量的 50% 以及消耗电力的三分之一。尽管匈牙利有重要...

reflection.en: Romans 8:22 reminds us that creation itself groans under the weight of change, a truth echoed in Europe's energy crisis caused by drought and heat. As natural systems face strain, communities experience the ripple effects, highlighting our interconnectedness with the environment. This situation calls for both wise stewardship and compassionate responses to...
reflection.zh: 罗马书8:22提醒我们，受造之物都在劳苦叹息，这在欧洲因干旱和高温引发的能源危机中得到了印证。当自然系统面临压力时，社区也感受到连锁反应，突显了我们与环境的相互关联。这种情况呼唤着明智的管理和对受这些挑战影响的人们作出富有同情心的回应。

verse.textEn: We know that the whole creation has been groaning as in the pains of childbirth right up to the present time.
verse.textZh: 我们知道，一切受造之物一同叹息、劳苦，直到如今。

title.en: The Mata Hari affair: Courtesan, spy, legend
title.zh: 玛塔·哈里事件：交际花、间谍、传奇

summary.en: Dancer Mata Hari, widely considered the most famous female spy in history, captivated many men but was ultimately executed for treason. The question of whether she truly betrayed state secrets remains a subject of historical debate.
summary.zh: 舞者玛塔·哈里被认为是历史上最著名的女间谍，她曾令无数男人倾倒，但最终因叛国罪被处决。她是否真的出卖了国家机密，至今仍是历史争论的焦点。

body.zh: 舞者玛塔·哈里被认为是有史以来最著名的女间谍，她让男人拜倒在她的脚下，但最终因叛国罪被处决。她真的泄露了国家机密吗？ 玛塔·哈里 (Mata Hari) 在她一生中就已经是一个传奇人物了。 1905 年，当她走进巴黎的聚光灯下时，她令上流社会为之倾倒。 巴黎媒体报道说：“她跳舞时只戴着面纱和镶满珠宝的紧身胸衣，几乎没有别的东西。” “从来没有人敢在如此颤抖的狂喜中赤身露面地出现在众神面前。她做出了多么美妙的动作——既大胆又端庄。” 玛塔·哈里让观众和媒体相信她是一位充满异国情调的寺庙舞者，但这位黑发表演者实际上是荷兰人。 美好时代的标志之一是巴黎人对异国文化的高度迷恋。在财务困境的驱使下，她通过假装印度人来利用这一需求。为了让自己的行为更加可信，她编造了一个背景故事，自称是一位德高望重的婆罗门的女儿。 “我的母亲是 Ranganathaswamy 寺庙的第一位舞者，她在我出生的那天十四岁那年去世。寺庙的祭司火化了她的尸体后，他们收养了我，并给我起名叫 Mata Hari，意思是‘白昼之眼’（马来语单词，Hari 的意思是太阳）。” 她声称从小就学习神圣的寺庙舞蹈。在她的表演过程中，面纱一层又一层地脱落。 后来她说：“我跳得不好，人们来看我的唯一原因是我是第一个敢于在公众面前裸露自己的人。” 上流社会对玛塔·哈里 (Mata Hari) 爱不释手，不知道她的真名是玛格丽特·吉尔特鲁伊达·泽勒 (Margaretha Geertruida Zelle)，而且她来自荷兰小镇吕伐登 (Leeuwarden)。 玛塔·哈里出生于 1876 年 8 月 7 日，是一位制帽匠的女儿，她通过股市投机致富。他经常用丰盛的礼物来宠爱他的女儿。在她六岁生日时，他送给她一辆山羊拉的马车。 13岁时，玛塔·哈里的奢华生活戛然而止。她的父亲破产并抛弃了家庭。两年后，母亲去世，她搬去亲戚家住。最终，她通过报纸广告认识了她的丈夫：“一名来自荷属东印度群岛（现为印度尼西亚）的军官，目前正在回籍假，寻求一位未来有结婚潜力的漂亮年轻女子的陪伴。财务状况无关紧要。” 玛塔·哈里 (Mata Hari) 和年长她 20 岁的苏格兰裔荷兰贵族约翰·鲁道夫·麦克劳德 (John Rudolf MacLeod) 很快就成为了情侣。 1897年，她随丈夫前往荷属东印度群岛。但她幸福生活的梦想从未实现。频繁的争吵使他们的关系变得紧张。然后，他们两岁的儿子……

reflection.en: The enduring question surrounding Mata Hari's guilt reminds us of the profound responsibility in judging others, especially when the full truth is obscured. Yahweh's call to self-reflection before condemnation encourages humility and compassion, urging us to consider the complexities of human actions and the weight of our verdicts. This perspective fosters...
reflection.zh: 围绕玛塔·哈里是否有罪的持久疑问，提醒我们在评判他人时所肩负的重大责任，尤其当真相模糊不清时。雅伟呼召我们在定罪前先自我反省，这鼓励我们保持谦卑和怜悯，敦促我们思考人类行为的复杂性以及我们判决的分量。这种视角促使我们以更仁慈的态度对待被指控者，承认我们自身的不足。

verse.textEn: Let any one of you who is without sin be the first to throw a stone at her.
verse.textZh: 你们中间谁是没有罪的，谁就可以先拿石头打她。

title.en: Can UN chief's initiative kickstart resolution for Cyprus?
title.zh: 联合国秘书长的倡议能否启动塞浦路斯问题的解决方案？

summary.en: UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres has launched a new diplomatic effort, believing a resolution to the Cyprus issue is crucial for regional stability. The initiative aims to explore the prospects for success in resolving the long-standing conflict.
summary.zh: 联合国秘书长安东尼奥·古特雷斯认为解决塞浦路斯问题对地区稳定至关重要，并已启动一项新的外交努力。该倡议旨在探讨其成功的可能性。

body.en:
UN chief Antonio Guterres considers a resolution to the Cyprus issue to be vital for regional stability and has initiated a new diplomatic effort. What are the prospects for its success?

UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres last week became the first UN chief to visit Cyprus in 16 years .

While there, he met the leaders of the island's two communities: Nikos Christodoulides, president of the Republic of Cyprus, and Tufan Erhurman , Turkish Cypriot leader and president of the self-declared Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus , which is only recognized by Turkey.

His aim in doing so was to determine whether the conditions exist for restarting negotiations on the Cyprus issue.

Progress on talks has remained stalled since the collapse of negotiations in Crans-Montana, Switzerland, in 2017, when the United Nations made its most comprehensive effort to broker a reunification agreement for the island.

According to diplomatic sources, the answer lies less in developments surrounding the Cyprus issue itself and more in the rapidly changing geopolitical landscape of the wider region.

War in the Middle East , deteriorating relations between Israel and Turkey , and growing strategic competition in the Eastern Mediterranean have heightened UN concerns that the unresolved Cyprus conflict could undermine the stability of the entire region.

Guterres said as much after the joint meeting on July 29. "I do believe that a solution in Cyprus is absolutely crucial, not only to preserve the interests and the peace of the Cyprus people, but also as a factor of stability in what is becoming a dangerously unstable region," he said.

Speaking to DW, Andreas Mavroyiannis, former permanent representative of the Republic of Cyprus to the United Nations and former chief negotiator of the Greek Cypriot side, shared the same concern.

"The strengthening of relations between the Republic of Cyprus and Israel , combined with the deterioration of Israel–Turkey relations, increases the risk of the Cyprus issue being instrumentalized," he told DW.

According to Mavroyiannis, the UN secretary-general fears that Cyprus could, instead of serving as a pillar of stability in the Middle East, become increasingly entangled in regional rivalries and emerge as one of the area's most vulnerable flashpoints.

The UN is not alone in viewing the Cyprus issue through the prism of regional security. The EU has also shown increasing interest in playing a more active political role in efforts to revive the peace process.

A significant step came on July 7, when the European Commission appointed Executive Vice-President Raffaele Fitto as the EU's Special Representative for the Cyprus issue.

body.zh: 联合国秘书长安东尼奥·古特雷斯认为塞浦路斯问题的解决对于地区稳定至关重要，并启动了新的外交努力。它的成功前景如何？ 联合国秘书长安东尼奥·古特雷斯上周成为 16 年来第一位访问塞浦路斯的联合国秘书长。 在那里，他会见了岛上两个社区的领导人：塞浦路斯共和国总统尼科斯·赫里斯托杜利德斯和土族塞人领导人兼自称为北塞浦路斯土耳其共和国（仅得到土耳其承认）的总统图凡·埃尔赫曼。 他这样做的目的是确定是否具备重启塞浦路斯问题谈判的条件。 自2017年瑞士克莱恩蒙塔纳谈判破裂以来，谈判进展一直停滞不前，当时联合国为促成该岛的统一协议做出了最全面的努力。 据外交消息人士透露，答案不在于塞浦路斯问题本身的事态发展，而在于更广泛地区迅速变化的地缘政治格局。 中东战争、以色列和土耳其关系恶化以及东地中海日益激烈的战略竞争加剧了联合国的担忧，即未解决的塞浦路斯冲突可能会破坏整个地区的稳定。 古特雷斯在 7 月 29 日的联席会议后说了同样的话。他说：“我确实相信，塞浦路斯问题的解决方案绝对至关重要，不仅可以维护塞浦路斯人民的利益与和平，而且可以作为这个正在变得危险不稳定的地区的稳定因素。” 塞浦路斯共和国前常驻联合国代表、希族塞人方面前首席谈判代表安德烈亚斯·马夫罗伊亚尼斯在接受德国之声采访时也表达了同样的担忧。 他对德国之声表示：“塞浦路斯共和国与以色列关系的加强，加上以色列与土耳其关系的恶化，增加了塞浦路斯问题被利用的风险。” 马夫罗伊亚尼斯表示，联合国秘书长担心塞浦路斯不仅不能成为中东稳定的支柱，反而会越来越多地卷入地区竞争，并成为该地区最脆弱的热点之一。 联合国并不是唯一一个从地区安全角度看待塞浦路斯问题的机构。欧盟也越来越有兴趣在恢复和平进程的努力中发挥更积极的政治作用。 7 月 7 日，欧盟委员会迈出重要一步，任命执行副主席拉斐尔·菲托 (Raffaele Fitto) 为欧盟塞浦路斯问题特别代表。 他的任务是支持联合国主导的进程，并加强欧盟的参与……

Yahweh's word encourages us to live at peace with everyone, as far as it depends on us, highlighting the ongoing responsibility to pursue reconciliation even amidst complex challenges. This pursuit, though often difficult,...
reflection.zh: 解决塞浦路斯问题等长期冲突的外交努力，提醒我们人类持续寻求和谐的呼召。雅伟的话语鼓励我们，只要力所能及，就要与所有人和平相处，这突显了即使在复杂的挑战中，也要持续追求和解的责任。这种追求，尽管常常困难重重，却反映了对地区稳定和人类福祉的承诺。

verse.textEn: If it is possible, as far as it depends on you, live at peace with everyone.
verse.textZh: 若是能行，总要尽力与众人和睦。

title.zh: 台湾总统为何在半夜被疏散？

summary.en: President William Lai participated in an emergency evacuation drill as part of Taiwan's military exercises, which are designed to prepare for a potential Chinese invasion.
summary.zh: 赖清德总统参加了台湾军事演习中的一次紧急疏散演练，旨在为潜在的中国入侵做准备。

body.en:
President William Lai took part in an emergency evacuation drill as part of Taiwan's annual Han Kuang military exercises that are running from August 5th to 14th.

The BBC’s Katy Watson explains what happened and why Taiwan is using the drills to prepare for a potential Chinese invasion.
body.zh: 总统赖清德参加了紧急疏散演习，这是台湾于8月5日至14日举行的年度汉光军事演习的一部分。 英国广播公司 (BBC) 的凯蒂·沃森 (Katy Watson) 解释了发生的事情以及台湾为何利用这些演习为中国潜在的入侵做准备。

reflection.en: In the face of looming threats and the need for preparedness, it is natural for nations and individuals to feel fear and dismay. Yet, Yahweh reminds us not to be afraid, promising His presence, strength, and help to uphold us. This divine assurance can bring a deep sense of peace even amidst uncertainty and drills for potential conflict.
reflection.zh: 面对迫在眉睫的威胁和备战的需要，国家和个人感到恐惧和沮丧是自然的。然而，雅伟提醒我们不要害怕，应许祂的同在、力量和帮助来扶持我们。即使在不确定性和潜在冲突的演习中，这种神圣的保证也能带来深刻的平安。

verse.textEn: So do not fear, for I am with you; do not be dismayed, for I am your God.
verse.textZh: 你不要害怕，因为我与你同在；不要惊惶，因为我是你的神。

title.en: Trump imposes 15% tariff on key chip material to counter China
title.zh: 特朗普对关键芯片材料征收15%关税以对抗中国

summary.en: The United States has imposed a 15% tariff on a crucial chip material, a measure aimed at safeguarding American companies from increasing competition within China's semiconductor industry.
summary.zh: 美国对一种关键芯片材料征收15%的关税，此举旨在保护美国公司免受中国芯片产业日益激烈的竞争。

body.en:
US President Donald Trump signed an executive order on Thursday that imposes a 15% tariff on imported products made from polysilicon, a crucial material used in semiconductors and solar panels.

The order also set minimum import prices on polysilicon and related products. It comes after a national security investigation into the production of the material overseas.

The move is intended to help protect US manufacturers as they face increasing competition from China's chip industry - a key source of friction between the world's two largest economies.

The Chinese embassy in Washington said the move "seriously disrupts" trade between the two countries and Beijing will act to protect its companies.

Washington is "abusing state power to go after Chinese businesses," the embassy said, adding that protectionism will not make the US more competitive.

Trump said in the order , external that he had accepted recommendations by Secretary of Commerce Howard Lutnick to set minimum import prices as well as a 15% tariff on polysilicon and related imports.

For decades, the US has allowed "foreign firms to weaken United States producers in the polysilicon sector," said Trump, who has long advocated for the use of tariffs to protect American jobs and boost the economy.

The material is critical in military equipment and electronics, yet imports have led to the US' share of global polysilicon production to fall from 50% in 2005 to less than 2% in 2024, Trump said.

The order is likely to benefit Hemlock Semiconductor and Wacker Chemie, which are the main producers of the material in the US.

The production of computer chips is central to the race between the US and China to develop artificial intelligence (AI). Washington and Beijing have also been locked in a tit-for-tat tariffs war , which has been on hold since May 2025.

Analysts quoted by Chinese state media outlet Global Times said the new tariff marks the latest escalation in Washington's efforts to limit China's role in critical technology supply chains.

The move follows other US restrictions on the imports of drones, humanoid robots and other tech products from China.

China announced a range of countermeasures this week, including tighter export controls on drones. Beijing also launched a national security review into imported printers and copiers.
body.zh: 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普周四签署了一项行政命令，对多晶硅制成的进口产品征收 15% 的关税，多晶硅是半导体和太阳能电池板中使用的关键材料。 该命令还规定了多晶硅及相关产品的最低进口价格。此前，国家安全部门对该材料的海外生产进行了调查。 此举旨在帮助保护美国制造商，因为它们面临着来自中国芯片行业日益激烈的竞争，而中国芯片行业是世界两大经济体之间摩擦的主要根源。 中国驻华盛顿大使馆表示，此举“严重扰乱”两国之间的贸易，北京将采取行动保护中国企业。 中国大使馆表示，华盛顿正在“滥用国家权力打压中国企业”，并补充说保护主义不会让美国更具竞争力。 特朗普在对外发布的命令中表示，他已接受商务部长霍华德·卢特尼克的建议，设定最低进口价格以及对多晶硅及相关进口产品征收 15% 的关税。 特朗普表示，几十年来，美国一直允许“外国公司削弱美国多晶硅行业的生产商”。他长期以来一直主张利用关税来保护美国就业并提振经济。 特朗普表示，这种材料在军事设备和电子产品中至关重要，但进口已导致美国在全球多晶硅产量中的份额从2005年的50%下降到2024年的不足2%。 该订单可能会使 Hemlock Semiconductor 和 Wacker Chemie 受益，它们是美国该材料的主要生产商。 计算机芯片的生产是中美发展人工智能（AI）竞赛的核心。华盛顿和北京也陷入了一场针锋相对的关税战，这场战争自 2025 年 5 月以来一直处于搁置状态。 中国官方媒体《环球时报》援引分析师的话称，新关税标志着华盛顿限制中国在关键技术供应链中的作用的最新升级。 此前，美国对从中国进口无人机、人形机器人和其他科技产品实施了其他限制。 中国本周宣布了一系列反制措施，包括加强对无人机的出口管制。北京还对进口打印机和复印机启动了国家安全审查。

reflection.en: In the pursuit of national economic advantage, it is easy to focus solely on human strategies and policies. This verse reminds us that true prosperity and the power to create wealth ultimately come from Yahweh. It encourages nations to remember their dependence on divine blessing even amidst global competition.
reflection.zh: 在追求国家经济优势的过程中，我们很容易只关注人类的策略和政策。这节经文提醒我们，真正的繁荣和创造财富的能力最终都来自雅伟。它鼓励各国即使在全球竞争中，也要记住对神圣祝福的依赖。

verse.textEn: Remember Yahweh your God, for it is he who gives you the ability to produce wealth.
verse.textZh: 你要记念雅伟你的神，因为得货财的力量是他给你的。

title.en: US to shut five consulates as critics fear China could fill diplomatic vacuum
title.zh: 美国将关闭五个领事馆，批评者担心中国可能填补外交真空

summary.en: The US State Department plans to close five foreign consulates and missions across Canada, Grenada, Japan, Indonesia, and Cameroon. This decision has drawn criticism, with concerns that it could create a diplomatic vacuum that other nations, such as China, might seek to fill.

body.en: State department informs Congress of planned closures in Canada, Grenada, Japan, Indonesia and Cameroon The US state department is to shut five foreign consulates and missions across Asia, Africa, North America and the Caribbean, drawing criticism that it is leaving a diplomatic vacuum at risk of being filled by China. The US Congress has been served notice of the impending closures, which are being justified on cost grounds and follow a reassessment of the US’s bilateral relationships with a range of countries since Donald Trump returned to the White House in January 2025. Proverbs 11:14 reminds us that where there is no guidance, a nation may falter, emphasizing the value of wise counsel and sustained diplomatic presence for global stability. verse.textEn: For lack of guidance a nation falls, but victory is won through many advisers.
verse.textZh: 无智谋，民就败落；谋士多，人便安居。

title.en: School-bus-sized SpaceX rocket chunk crashes into Moon
title.zh: 校车大小的SpaceX火箭残骸坠毁月球

summary.en: A school-bus-sized chunk of a SpaceX rocket has crashed into the Moon, raising concerns among experts about increasing lunar debris. This incident occurs amidst a growing space race between the United States and China to send humans back to the Moon.
summary.zh: 一块校车大小的SpaceX火箭残骸坠毁在月球上，引发专家对月球垃圾日益增多的担忧。此事发生在中美两国竞相将人类送回月球之际。

body.en:
A piece of a SpaceX rocket that has been floating in space for the past year has slammed into the moon, according to scientists.

Although no-one observed the collision, a telescope in Chile spotted what astronomers have identified as a debris plume resulting from the crash.

Space tracking experts said it was inevitable that the leftover rocket segment would plough into the moon .

The school-bus-sized object is the second stage ‌of a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket that had launched a lunar lander from Firefly Aerospace toward the moon in January 2025.

Weighing 4,000kg, the rocket piece had been due to hit the moon at around 4.35pm AEST on Wednesday, travelling at around 8,690km/h.

It's the latest instance of lunar litter — rubbish left behind on the moon — that some experts believe could become a greater concern as the United States and China race to put astronauts on the moon .

In 2022, a Chinese rocket unintentionally hit the moon following a lunar mission, and more stray rocket pieces could have struck the moon in past decades without scientists' knowledge.

Julianna Scheiman, director of Dragon Human Spaceflight at SpaceX, said the company is working with NASA to avoid future wrecks.

She also emphasised that the projected crash was not deliberate. A combination of solar activity and gravity accidentally put it on a collision course with the moon, according to Scheiman.

Carl Schmidt, a planetary scientist at Boston University, said he is "100 per cent certain" that his team's observations revealed signs of the lunar crash.

The European Southern Observatory's Very Large Telescope also detected a stream of sodium and lithium stretching for tens of kilometres into space for at least five to 10 minutes following the impact, Schmidt added.

"We don't have images of the impact", but there is telescope evidence, Schmidt said in email correspondence shared with media.

Even before signs of the debris plume were spotted by the telescope in Chile, retired astrophysicist Jonathan McDowell noted that observations of the dead upper stage on Tuesday night showed it heading straight for the moon.

The anticipated crash site was a dusty, barren patch near Einstein Crater on the moon's sunlit western limb — near the edge of the near and far sides, which is especially difficult to observe from Earth.

"There's no doubt in my mind" that the rocket "is now in teeny, little pieces scattered over the moon near Einstein Crater", McDowell said.

body.zh: 据科学家称，过去一年一直漂浮在太空中的 SpaceX 火箭的一块碎片撞上了月球。 尽管没有人观察到这次碰撞，但智利的一架望远镜发现了天文学家认为是碰撞产生的碎片羽流。 太空跟踪专家表示，剩余的火箭部分不可避免地会撞向月球。 这个校车大小的物体是 SpaceX Falcon 9 火箭的第二级，该火箭于 2025 年 1 月从 Firefly Aerospace 向月球发射了月球着陆器。 这枚重 4,000 公斤的火箭原定于周三下午 4.35 左右（澳大利亚东部标准时间）撞击月球，飞行速度约为 8,690 公里/小时。 您值得信赖的来源，让您了解周围世界的最新动态。直接将免费的每日新闻更新和分析发送到您的收件箱。 这是月球垃圾（留在月球上的垃圾）的最新实例，一些专家认为，随着美国和中国竞相将宇航员送上月球，这可能会成为一个更大的问题。 2022 年，一枚中国火箭在完成探月任务后无意中撞上了月球，而在过去的几十年里，更多的火箭碎片可能在科学家不知情的情况下撞上了月球。 SpaceX 龙人航天项目主管朱莉安娜·谢曼 (Julianna Scheiman) 表示，该公司正在与 NASA 合作，以避免未来发生残骸。 她还强调，预计的坠机事故并非故意。谢曼表示，太阳活动和重力的结合意外地使其与月球发生了碰撞。 波士顿大学行星科学家卡尔·施密特表示，他“百分百确定”他的团队的观察揭示了月球坠毁的迹象。 施密特补充说，欧洲南方天文台的甚大望远镜还探测到，在撞击发生后，钠和锂的流向太空延伸了数十公里，持续了至少五到十分钟。 施密特在与媒体分享的电子邮件中表示，“我们没有撞击的图像”，但有望远镜证据。 甚至在智利的望远镜发现碎片羽流的迹象之前，退休天体物理学家乔纳森·麦克道尔就指出，周二晚上对死亡的上级的观测表明它直奔月球。 预期的坠机地点是月球阳光照射下的西翼爱因斯坦陨石坑附近一片尘土飞扬、贫瘠的地方——靠近近侧和远侧的边缘，从地球上观测到这一点尤其困难。 麦克道尔说，“在我看来，毫无疑问”火箭“现在已经变成了微小的碎片，散落在月球上靠近爱因斯坦陨石坑的地方”。 观星者知道，从地面上看到从形成的陨石坑中喷出的尘埃和岩石羽流，即使不是不可能，也是很困难的，更不用说闪光了……

reflection.en: As humanity extends its reach to the Moon, this incident reminds us that our actions have consequences beyond Earth. Psalm 24:1 declares that "The earth is Yahweh's, and everything in it, the world, and all who live in it," a principle that calls us to responsible stewardship of all creation, near and far. reflection.zh: 当人类将足迹延伸至月球时，这起事件提醒我们，我们的行为对地球之外同样产生影响。诗篇24:1宣告：“地和其中所充满的，世界和住在其间的，都属雅伟。”这一原则呼吁我们对所有受造物，无论远近，都负起负责任的管家职分。我们探索新领域的雄心，应与保护其原始面貌的承诺相平衡，以反映其神圣所有者的关怀。

verse.textEn: The earth is Yahweh's, and everything in it, the world, and all who live in it.
verse.textZh: 地和其中所充满的，世界和住在其间的，都属雅伟。

title.en: Democracy is at stake when foolish humans bet on machines being intelligent | Rafael Behr
title.zh: 当愚蠢的人类押注机器智能时，民主就岌岌可危 | 拉斐尔·贝尔

summary.en: The article argues that democracy is jeopardized when human leaders unwisely place their trust in artificial intelligence. It highlights the critical need for enlightened leadership, particularly from the US president, to advocate for global AI regulation, contrasting this need with current political realities.
summary.zh: 文章指出，当人类领导者不明智地将信任寄托于人工智能时，民主就会受到威胁。它强调了开明领导人（特别是美国总统）推动全球人工智能监管的迫切需求，并将其与当前的政治现实进行了对比。

body.en: We need an enlightened US president to make the case for global AI regulation. Donald Trump is the exact opposite of what is needed When I am woken by the sound of my dog whining, I understand that she is hungry and wants me to get up. When my alarm clock goes off, I don’t consider its needs. It is following an instruction to rouse me at a certain time but it doesn’t care if I stay in bed. It doesn’t try to get me up by other means. The dog, on the other hand, will go to plan B. She barks. This capacity for autonomous action was once a difference between animals and machines. AI has blurred the line . Advanced models devise their own strategies to reach a goal. The task might be defined by a human master, but the machine weighs its options for delivery. It can make its own choices. Given rules, it can break them. Continue reading...
body.zh: 我们需要一位开明的美国总统来为全球人工智能监管提供理由。唐纳德·特朗普与我们所需要的恰恰相反。当我被狗的哀鸣声吵醒时，我知道她饿了，想让我起床。当我的闹钟响起时，我不会考虑它的需求。它会按照指令在特定时间叫醒我，但它并不关心我是否留在床上。它不会试图通过其他方式让我起床。另一方面，狗会执行 B 计划。她会吠叫。这种自主行动的能力曾经是动物和机器之间的区别。人工智能已经模糊了界限。先进的模型会制定自己的策略来实现目标。该任务可能由人类主人定义，但机器会权衡其交付选项。它可以做出自己的选择。既定规则，它可能会打破它们。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence challenges us to consider the limits of human understanding and the wisdom needed to govern powerful new technologies. As we navigate this complex future, Yahweh's word reminds us not to lean solely on our own intellect or creations, but to seek a deeper, divine wisdom. True discernment comes from trusting in...
reflection.zh: 人工智能的迅速发展促使我们思考人类理解的局限性，以及管理强大新兴科技所需的智慧。当我们驾驭这个复杂的未来时，雅伟的话语提醒我们不要单单依靠自己的智力或创造物，而要寻求更深层的、来自雅伟的智慧。真正的洞察力来自于全心信靠雅伟，尤其是在面对影响社会根基的决策时。

verse.textEn: Trust in Yahweh with all your heart and lean not on your own understanding.
verse.textZh: 你要专心仰赖雅伟，不可倚靠自己的聪明。

title.en: A moment that changed me: I found a forbidden novel – it led to a dangerous, lasting love
title.zh: 一个改变我的时刻：我发现了一本禁书——它带来了一段危险而持久的爱

summary.en: A Uyghur woman recounts how finding a forbidden novel in Xinjiang led her to embrace her culture and a lasting love, despite societal disapproval.
summary.zh: 一位维吾尔族女性讲述了她在新疆发现一本禁书后，如何因此拥抱自己的文化并找到一份持久的爱，尽管这在社会上受到非议。

body.en: Growing up in the Chinese region of Xinjiang, romance was frowned upon – as was much of my Uyghur culture. But one day, exploring a strange house, I found a gateway to both worlds Many people have a book that changes their life. For me and my wife, one book in particular changed our destinies for ever. We have been in love since we were teenagers, and today we are happily married – all because I accidentally discovered a forbidden novel in someone else’s house. It was a hot summer’s evening in 2009, in Kumul, Xinjiang. I was 16 and my father insisted I accompany him to visit a distant relative, where they would spend hours chatting about the old days and feasting as if they hadn’t eaten in years. As the well-behaved teenager I tried to be, I sat politely, nodding at their stories and pretending to absorb their “life lessons”, attempting to hide my boredom. The living room, with its small windows and bright lighting, was unbearable. Continue reading...
body.zh: 我在中国新疆地区长大，浪漫是不受欢迎的——就像我的维吾尔文化一样。但有一天，在探索一栋陌生的房子时，我发现了通往两个世界的大门许多人都有一本改变他们生活的书。对于我和我的妻子来说，有一本书永远改变了我们的命运。我们从少年时就相爱，到今天幸福地结婚了——这一切都是因为我无意中在别人家里发现了一本禁书。 2009年，新疆哈密尔一个炎热的夏夜。我当时 16 岁，父亲坚持让我陪他去拜访一位远房亲戚，他们会花上几个小时谈论过去的时光，然后大吃大喝，就好像他们已经很多年没有吃饭一样了。作为一个我努力成为的乖孩子，我礼貌地坐着，对他们的故事点头，假装吸收他们的“人生教训”，试图隐藏我的无聊。客厅的窗户很小，灯光明亮，令人难以忍受。继续阅读...

reflection.en: This story highlights the courage to follow one's heart and embrace one's identity, even when cultural norms or authorities forbid it. It reminds us that there are times when our deepest convictions, aligned with Yahweh's truth, call us to a path different from what human systems dictate.
reflection.zh: 这个故事彰显了追随内心、拥抱自我身份的勇气，即便文化规范或权威禁止。它提醒我们，有时我们最深刻的信念，与雅伟的真理相符，会召唤我们走一条不同于人类体系所规定的道路。

verse.textEn: We must obey God rather than human beings!
verse.textZh: 顺从神，不顺从人，是应当的。

title.en: Trump administration reportedly drafting ban on Chinese datacenter components

summary.en: The Trump administration is reportedly preparing a ban on US imports of new Chinese datacenter components. This measure, being developed by the FCC, signals an effort by US authorities to address concerns related to technology and trade.

title.en: From petitions to memes: How students made dissent visible
title.zh: 从请愿到网络迷因：学生如何让异议显现

summary.en: Student movements throughout history, from imperial China to modern India, have consistently found new ways to express dissent and challenge established authority, adapting their methods to contemporary tools and symbols.
summary.zh: 从中国古代到当今印度，学生运动不断调整其工具和象征，以挑战权威，使异议得以显现。

body.en:
From imperial China to present-day India, student movements have repeatedly adapted the tools and symbols of their age to challenge authority.

On July 22, 2026, in rainy Mumbai, India , a casually dressed young woman stepped in front of a slow-moving police van carrying detained students. She placed her palm on the hood, forcing the vehicle to stop.

Mobile phones captured the moment from every angle. She too, raised her own phone and recorded the encounter. Within hours, the clip spread across India and beyond.

It became one of the defining visuals of the Cockroach Janta Party protests, a movement in which students demanded transparency and accountability, following leaks in India's medical entrance exams.

But the power of the moment lay not only in what she did, but in how quickly it was seen. A single gesture, a young woman confronting authority , became a symbol shared across millions of screens.

While the clip belongs to a generation raised on social media, the impulse behind it is much older.

From court petitions and revolutionary posters to photographs, umbrellas and memes, student movements have repeatedly adapted the tools and symbols available to them, turning them into vehicles for dissent.

Long before television or social media carried dissent across borders, students still found ways to make their grievances heard.

In Eastern Han China, for instance, scholars at the Imperial Academy (Taixue) aligned with reform-minded officials in opposing powerful eunuchs at court, whom many viewed as corrupt and politically overbearing.

They voiced their objections through public criticism, political networks and petitions.

In an era when political communication moved through official channels, petitions were among the established ways of bringing grievances before the throne. Written in formal language and delivered through the bureaucracy, they carried student concerns directly into the state's communication system.

In Paris in 1968, students challenged university authorities and a conservative postwar social order. As demonstrations spread across the French capital and drew in workers, one of the movement's most enduring contributions emerged from a basement workshop at the Ecole des Beaux-Arts.

The Atelier Populaire ("People's Workshop") printed thousands of posters during the protests, many of them overnight. Their bold graphics, silhouettes and slogans became the visual language of the movement. Produced collectively, many carried no individual author's name, helping transform protest into a shared public voice.

The posters and their messages could appear in dozens of places overnight, giving the protest a wide local visual presence.

Protests also became more impactful when images could be transmitted across borders.

body.zh: 从中华帝国到当今的印度，学生运动不断地采用他们那个时代的工具和符号来挑战权威。 2026 年 7 月 22 日，在多雨的印度孟买，一名穿着休闲的年轻女子走到一辆载着被拘留学生的缓慢行驶的警车前。她将手掌放在引擎盖上，迫使车辆停了下来。 手机从各个角度捕捉了这一时刻。她也举起了自己的手机，记录了这次遭遇。几个小时内，这段视频就传遍了印度及其他地区。 它成为蟑螂简塔党抗议活动的标志性视觉效果之一，在印度医学入学考试泄密后，学生们在这场运动中要求透明度和问责制。 但这一刻的​​力量不仅在于她所做的事情，还在于她的所作所为很快被人们看到。一个年轻女子对抗权威的一个动作，成为了数百万屏幕上共享的符号。 虽然这段视频属于在社交媒体上长大的一代人，但其背后的冲动却要古老得多。 从法庭请愿书和革命海报到照片、雨伞和模因，学生运动不断地调整他们可用的工具和符号，将它们变成异议的工具。 早在电视或社交媒体跨境传播异议之前，学生们就已经找到了表达不满的方法。 例如，在中国东汉，太学的学者与具有改革思想的官员结盟，反对宫廷中有权有势的宦官，许多人认为宦官腐败且在政治上专横。 他们通过公开批评、政治网络和请愿来表达他们的反对意见。 在政治沟通通过官方渠道进行的时代，请愿是向王室表达不满的既定方式之一。它们以正式语言编写并通过官僚机构传达，将学生的担忧直接传达到国家的沟通系统中。 1968 年的巴黎，学生们挑战大学当局和保守的战后社会秩序。随着示威活动在法国首都蔓延并吸引了工人，该运动最持久的贡献之一来自巴黎美术学院的一个地下室工作室。 Atelier Populaire（“人民工作室”）在抗议期间印制了数千张海报，其中许多是在一夜之间印制的。他们大胆的图形、轮廓和口号成为了这场运动的视觉语言。许多作品都是集体制作的，没有作者的名字，这有助于将抗议转变为公众的共同声音。 这些海报及其信息可能会在一夜之间出现在数十个地方，使抗议活动在当地得到广泛的关注。 当图像可以跨境传输时，抗议的影响力也变得更大。 在...

Yahweh, through the prophet Amos, calls for justice to flow powerfully and consistently, reminding us that true righteousness should be an undeniable force in society. This pursuit of a more just world often requires courage to speak truth to...

title.en: US-China AI rivalry heats up as Chinese models gain ground
title.zh: 中美人工智能竞争加剧，中国模型迎头赶上

summary.en: China's AI platforms are rapidly advancing, narrowing the gap with US technology. This progress has led to renewed threats from the Trump administration, alongside accusations of intellectual property theft, raising concerns about escalating tensions between the two nations.
summary.zh: 中国的人工智能平台正迅速缩小与美国同行的差距。这一进展引发了特朗普政府新的威胁，并伴随着知识产权盗窃的指控，令人担忧两国之间的紧张关系可能升级。

body.en:
China's AI platforms are rapidly closing the gap with their US counterparts, prompting fresh threats from the Trump administration. With accusations of intellectual property theft, could tensions boil over?

In what seems like the blink of an eye,  China has gone from being up to five years behind the United States in top-tier artificial intelligence (AI) to lagging by just a few months.

While US players, including Anthropic's Claude and OpenAI's ChatGPT , have spent hundreds of billions of dollars to push the frontier of AI, China has pursued a very different path .

Faced with US curbs on high-end chips that help AI to do its most advanced thinking, Chinese tech firms have prioritized dozens of open-source AI models built on "good enough"  technology .

These platforms, including DeepSeek, Alibaba's Qwen and Xiaomi's MiMo, are now widely deployed across Chinese businesses, government services and consumer devices.

In the latest sign of the gap closing, Chinese startup Moonshot AI last week unveiled Kimi K3, a model that rivals one of the most advanced AI models — Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 — on key benchmarks.

In some tests, Kimi K3 matches or even surpasses Claude with far less computing power and at a fraction of the cost. 

Global technology specialist Alvin W. Graylin thinks Kimi K3's arrival turns high-end AI from an expensive luxury into something practical and affordable.

"For 98% of customers, the 1 to 2% difference [in knowledge] isn't worth paying 10 to 20 times more."

China's latest advance has already drawn a strong reaction from Washington, with US President Donald Trump now threatening to block US access to Chinese AI models.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, meanwhile, warned earlier this week that the US could sanction Chinese models over alleged intellectual property (IP) theft.

Anthropic  and OpenAI have accused Chinese labs of using their models to train their own systems, a process known as distilling.

While distilling is a common practice by AI labs worldwide to a limited extent, the companies say their models have been bombarded with queries to harvest advanced reasoning. The White House warned in April that China was doing it on an "industrial scale."

Beijing has hit back, rejecting the accusations as baseless and calling US threats of sanctions and model bans "technological bullying" to contain China's rise.

Giulia Neaher, a research analyst at the Strategic Foresight Hub at the Washington-based Stimson Center think tank, downplayed the role of distilling in Kimi's progress.

body.zh: 中国的人工智能平台正在迅速缩小与美国同行的差距，引发了特朗普政府的新威胁。随着知识产权盗窃的指控，紧张局势会升级吗？ 似乎一眨眼的功夫，中国在顶级人工智能 (AI) 领域就从落后美国五年变为仅落后几个月。 尽管包括 Anthropic 的 Claude 和 OpenAI 的 ChatGPT 在内的美国企业已经花费了数千亿美元来推动人工智能的前沿发展，但中国却走了一条截然不同的道路。 面对美国对帮助人工智能实现最先进思维的高端芯片的限制，中国科技公司优先考虑了数十种基于“足够好”技术的开源人工智能模型。 这些平台，包括 DeepSeek、阿里巴巴的 Qwen 和小米的 MiMo，现已广泛部署在中国企业、政府服务和消费设备中。 作为缩小差距的最新迹象，中国初创公司 Moonshot AI 上周推出了 Kimi K3，该模型在关键基准测试上可与最先进的人工智能模型之一——Anthropic 的 Claude Fable 5 相媲美。 在某些测试中，Kimi K3 可以与 Claude 相媲美甚至超过 Claude，但其计算能力却要低得多，而成本却只是 Claude 的一小部分。 全球技术专家 Alvin W. Graylin 认为 Kimi K3 的到来将高端人工智能从昂贵的奢侈品变成了实用且负担得起的东西。 “对于 98% 的客户来说，[知识] 1% 到 2% 的差异并不值得多付 10 到 20 倍的费用。” 中国的最新进展已经引起华盛顿的强烈反应，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普现在威胁要阻止美国使用中国的人工智能模型。 与此同时，财政部长斯科特·贝森特本周早些时候警告称，美国可能会因涉嫌盗窃知识产权而制裁中国模型。 Anthropic 和 OpenAI 指责中国实验室使用他们的模型来训练他们自己的系统，这一过程被称为蒸馏。 虽然提炼是全球人工智能实验室在一定程度上的常见做法，但这些公司表示，他们的模型已经受到查询的轰炸，以收获高级推理。白宫四月份警告说，中国正在以“工业规模”这样做。 北京方面予以反击，否认这些指控毫无根据，并称美国威胁实施制裁和示范禁令是“技术欺凌”，旨在遏制中国的崛起。 华盛顿智库史汀生中心战略远见中心的研究分析师朱莉娅·尼赫（Giulia Neaher）淡化了提炼在基米进步中的作用。 “[其成功]很大程度上归功于为建设这个项目而投入的人才、基础设施和资源......

title.en: Attorney general warns women and children at risk of ‘harmful conduct’ from smartglasses users – as it happened
title.zh: 司法部长警告智能眼镜用户可能对妇女和儿童造成‘有害行为’

summary.en: Australia's Attorney General has issued a warning regarding the potential for “harmful conduct” against women and children by users of smartglasses. The statement underscores concerns about new technologies and their implications for public safety.
summary.zh: 澳大利亚司法部长就智能眼镜用户可能对妇女和儿童造成的“有害行为”发出了警告。该声明强调了对新技术及其对公共安全影响的担忧。

body.en:
The attorney general, Michelle Rowland , has written to the privacy commissioner over potential concerns surrounding smartglasses.

Rowland said the products, which are growing in popularity, had significant implications, especially for women and children who could be disproportionately affected by “inappropriate recording, harassment, surveillance or other harmful conduct”.

Privacy is an essential part of all our lives; it allows us to be who we are with dignity and without fear.

Unlike other forms of technology, smart glasses may be used more discreetly, making it harder to know when you are being recorded.

The government is continuing to work on the next phase of privacy reforms to ensure our privacy laws are fit for purpose in the digital age.
body.zh: 司法部长米歇尔·罗兰 (Michelle Rowland) 已就智能眼镜的潜在担忧致信隐私专员。 罗兰表示，这些产品越来越受欢迎，具有重大影响，特别是对于妇女和儿童来说，他们可能会受到“不当录音、骚扰、监视或其他有害行为”的严重影响。 隐私是我们生活的重要组成部分；它让我们能够有尊严、毫无恐惧地做自己。 与其他形式的技术不同，智能眼镜的使用可能会更加谨慎，因此更难知道您何时被录音。 政府正在继续致力于下一阶段的隐私改革，以确保我们的隐私法适合数字时代的目的。

reflection.en: The Attorney General's warning highlights the need to protect vulnerable individuals, particularly women and children, from emerging technological harms. Proverbs 31:8-9 reminds us of the moral imperative to speak for those who cannot speak for themselves, ensuring justice for all. This principle calls us to advocate for safety and dignity in an evolving...

title.en: Are you owed a share of $274 million in unclaimed money? Here's how to check
title.zh: 你是否应得2.74亿澳元无人认领款项中的一份？这里教你如何查询。

summary.en: Nearly one million Australians are reportedly owed a share of $274 million in unclaimed money, with the average amount per person being around $280.
summary.zh: 据报道，近一百万澳大利亚人有权获得总计2.74亿澳元的无人认领款项，平均每人约280澳元。

body.en:
Hundreds of millions of dollars are waiting to be claimed by Australians who have not provided their current bank account details to Services Australia.

The agency says 974,000 Australians are owed a slice of $274.5 million in unpaid Medicare benefits.

It's urging people to check that their bank details are up to date in their Medicare online account.

Young Australians account for the largest share, with more than $65 million payable to 255,000 people aged between 18 and 24.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

A Services Australia spokesperson advises Australians to update their personal details with Medicare when they change bank or address.

To receive Medicare benefits, Services Australia needs your bank account details.

To check whether you're owed money, log in to your myGov account, or create one if you don't have one.

Then, check that your bank details are up to date. You'll need to provide your BSB, account number, and account name.

Once you've provided the required information, if you're owed money, any unpaid Medicare benefits will usually be paid into your account within three days.

If you're not comfortable completing the process online, you can contact the Medicare line on 132 011 or visit a service centre to update your bank details.

The Australian Taxation Office (ATO) said in October there were seven million Australians who could be owed a share of a $19 billion pool of lost and unclaimed superannuation.

Other sources of unclaimed money include deceased estates, lost share dividends, wages, cheques, overpayments and more.

For the latest from SBS News, download our app and subscribe to our newsletter .

title.en: Why one tiny island's Census is about much more than numbers
title.zh: 为什么一个小岛的人口普查不仅仅是数字

summary.en: It's been a decade since Norfolk Island was first counted in the Census. The milestone may not be celebrated by everyone.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及盼望、忍耐与重建。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
In the middle of the South Pacific Ocean, a tiny island spanning just 35 square kilometres will be included in this year's Census .

Home to about 2,100 residents, Norfolk Island has earned a reputation as "one of the most beautiful places on Earth", according to acting general manager of the Norfolk Island Regional Council (NIRC), Nicholas Mostardo.

He moved to the subtropical island early this year and says its natural beauty and close-knit community make it unlike anywhere else.

"It's got a rich environment, it's got very warm and kind people. It's probably one of the most unique places in the world that I've had personally the pleasure of being involved with," Mostardo told SBS News.

NIRC is currently under administration until 31 December 2026, as Norfolk Island transitions to what the Australian government has described as a "new bespoke governance model".

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

In the interim, Mostardo has been liaising with the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) to help ensure Norfolk Island's population is recorded during the Census of Population and Housing on 11 August.

"We've had several visits from the ABS zone manager and the assistant director of Census Mainstream and Enumeration. They've been coming out to ensure the community is well engaged and consulted on completing the form."

The Census has been conducted in Australia for more than a century , but this will be the third time Norfolk Island has ever participated in the survey. It also marks a decade since the Australian government passed reforms that led to the island being included in the Census.

In 1914, Norfolk became an Australian territory, but the "precise constitutional arrangement was not clear at the time", according to an online statement by legal advisory firm Norfolk Advisory.

Around 65 years later, the Australian parliament allowed Norfolk Islanders to form a limited self-government. Following governance reforms passed in 2015 and implemented in 2016, the Australian government assumed responsibility for the island's governance.

In 2023, Norfolk Island regained some involvement in its affairs through the establishment of a new advisory body, the Norfolk Island Governance Committee. The island is now considered an external territory of Australia.

This complex history has divided some people — including those of Pitcairn descent — about whether Norfolk Island should be counted during Australia's Census.

Israel's ambassador to Australia has defended his embassy's unusual public intervention ahead of Labor's national conference last month, rejecting suggestions it sought to influence the party's platform and insisting it was merely providing information to decision-makers.

In a rare step, the Israeli embassy issued a lengthy statement ahead of the conference in Adelaide, taking issue with Labor's proposed position on the Israeli-Palestinian conflict.

The embassy argued Labor's draft national platform placed responsibility for the conflict on Israel while overlooking the role of Hamas and Palestinian leadership.

It sparked criticism from pro-Palestinian advocates that Israel was inappropriately interfering in Australian politics.

Speaking to SBS Hebrew on Thursday, Israeli ambassador Hillel Newman said "we had no intention and no actual intervention".

"All we did was we put forth facts for the decision-makers to have before them in making educated decisions," he said.

"We are just a resource of some kind in giving the information. We did not intervene in the convention itself. We do not intervene in the process. We just brought information to the knowledge of the decision-makers.

"The Palestinian envoys here also had some things to say about the ALP platform and convention, and no-one said it's foreign intervention," he said.

At the time, the Australia Palestine Advocacy Network (APAN), an advocacy group, condemned what it called an "extraordinary intervention" by the Israeli embassy and described it as "an unacceptable attempt by a foreign government to influence Australia’s domestic political processes".

"If the Israeli regime believes Labor's platform is too critical while Gaza is being destroyed, perhaps it should reflect on its own conduct rather than attempting to pressure an Australian political party," APAN president Nasser Mashni said.

Mashni said the draft platform fell "far short of taking appropriate action to recognise the Palestinian genocide".

Israel has been accused of genocide by a United Nations inquiry, an allegation it denies. Its prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, is the subject of an International Criminal Court (ICC) arrest warrant over alleged war crimes and crimes against humanity, which Israel rejects.

The Labor platform is debated at its national conference to determine the party's positions on a broad range of issues. Its 2026 draft reflected shifts and an expanded position on Israel and Palestine since its last iteration in 2023.

The government decided to recognise Palestinian statehood in September last year.

title.en: Why Australia could be heading for a spring and summer 'triple whammy'

summary.en: The article discusses the potential for Australia to experience a "triple whammy" of extreme weather during its upcoming spring and summer seasons, drawing parallels with record-breaking heat observed in the northern hemisphere.

body.en:
Three climate forces are lining up ahead of spring, raising the odds of hotter and drier weather across parts of Australia.

The world is facing a potentially record-breaking El Niño , with the Bureau of Meteorology (BoM) forecasting it will continue to intensify into a "very strong event" that may persist well into next year.

At the same time, another Australian climate driver associated with warmer and drier conditions — a positive Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD) — is expected to develop by spring.

"So, for Australia through the coming spring and summer, the double whammy of climate change and El Niño will be driving our weather. In actual fact, we might even have a triple whammy," Andrew Watkins, an adjunct professor at Monash University and a Climate Council researcher, told SBS News.

"Unfortunately, that pattern really sets in until summer, when the Asian monsoon comes in and knocks it over. But if we have climate change and El Niño and a positive Indian Ocean dipole, they are three things that all push south-east Australia into hotter and drier, and especially the spring period," he said.

While an El Niño does not necessarily mean hotter and drier conditions for Australia, it does raise the likelihood.

As parts of Europe and the United States swelter through a summer of scorching heatwaves and fires, BoM climatologist Zhi-Weng Chua says soon, much of Australia will likely swelter too.

He says there is a high chance much of the nation's south-east and south-west will experience one of the warmest springs on record.

"Western parts of Western Australia, extending into southern Queensland and parts of south Australia, there is a strong indication that temperatures will be in the top 20 per cent of historical records for spring," he told SBS News.

But the heat expected during Australia's spring and summer are driven by different factors to those pushing temperatures skyward in Europe and North America.

Those continents have experienced the impact of climate change in the past few months, with record-high temperatures leading to high fire danger.

El Niño is an event measured by the sea surface temperature of the Pacific Ocean — it has a strong impact on the Asia Pacific, but far less on Europe and North America.

Sea surface temperatures in the central Pacific are now more than 2C above average — a level associated with a very strong El Niño — for the first time in a decade.

title.en: 'Racism is like a cancer': Senator Lidia Thorpe joins growing calls for royal commission

body.en:
Indigenous senator Lidia Thorpe has warned racism is "like a cancer", as she joins lobbying efforts to hold a national royal commission into how it impacts Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples.

Influential Northern Land Council chairman Matthew Ryan also pushed for the issue to be elevated to the highest level of national inquiry, after giving evidence to a parliamentary committee investigating racism, hate and violence towards Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander People.

He told the Labor-led inquiry the Northern Territory Country Liberal Party (CLP) government's child removal policy, Indigenous over-representation in prison and the suicide rate equated to "modern day slavery".

At the Garma Festival in North East Arnhem Land last weekend, he told reporters the parliamentary inquiry had exposed systemic racism.
